sections.title: Surgical Technique Selection Algorithm
content: 1. Assess Levator Function (LF): If LF < 4mm, proceed to Frontalis Sling.
2. Phenylephrine Test (2.5% or 10%): If lid elevates to desired level and LF is good (>10mm), consider Müller Muscle-Conjunctival Resection (MMCR).
3. Levator Function 5-10mm: External Levator Advancement or Resection is the gold standard.
4. High Crease + Thinned Lid: Suggests Aponeurotic Ptosis; perform Levator Aponeurosis Repair.
5. Marcus-Gunn Jaw Winking: Requires Levator Excision followed by Frontalis Sling.

sections.title: Hering's Law Warning
content: Hering’s Law of Equal Innervation: Lifting a more ptotic lid can cause the contralateral lid to drop.
Always perform the 'Manual Elevation Test' in the clinic.
Warn patients with bilateral ptosis that two surgeries might be needed.
Document Hering's response preoperative to manage expectations.

sections.title: Müller's Muscle-Conjunctival Resection (MMCR)
content: 1. Confirm 2mm+ response to Phenylephrine.
2. Evert the eyelid with a Desmarres retractor.
3. Mark and clamp 1/2 the amount of measured lid elevation (Putterman technique).
4. Suture (6-0 plain gut or Prolene) under the Putterman clamp.
5. Resect the tissue above the clamp and bury knots to avoid keratopathy.

sections.title: External Levator Advancement Steps
content: 1. Incise along the eyelid crease skin marking.
2. Dissect through orbicularis to expose the orbital septum.
3. Open the septum to reveal the preaponeurotic fat pad (key landmark).
4. Identify the levator aponeurosis below the fat pad.
5. Secure aponeurosis to superior 1/3 of tarsus with 6-0 Silk/Prolene sutures.
6. Intraoperative adjustment: Patient sits up to check height and contour.

sections.title: Frontalis Sling: Materials & Methods
content: Indication: LF < 4mm or Neurogenic ptosis.
Materials: Autologous Fascia Lata (Gold Standard), Silicone rod (reversible/adjustable), Supramid.
Configuration: Fox Pentagon or Crawford Open technique.
Placement: From the tarsus to the frontalis muscle (eyebrow).
Outcome: Eyelid is raised by the power of the forehead/frontalis muscle.

sections.title: Emergency 'Red Flags' in Ptosis
content: New onset ptosis + Miosis = Horner Syndrome (Rule out Carotid Artery Dissection).
New onset ptosis + Mydriasis = 3rd Nerve Palsy (Rule out P-Comm Aneurysm).
Variable ptosis + Diplopia = Myasthenia Gravis (Order Ice Test/AChR antibodies).
Congenital Ptosis + Poor Visual Acuity = Amblyopia risk (Urgent surgery needed).

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
sections.content: Recent shifts favor minimally invasive 'Internal' Levator Advancement (M-ILA) to avoid skin scars. The use of Oxymetazoline 0.1% (Upneeq) provides a non-surgical alternative for mild acquired ptosis by stimulating Müller's muscle. 3D-printed templates for fascia lata harvesting and adjustable suture techniques are becoming more prevalent in complex tertiary referrals.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls: The Master Surgeon's Tips
content: Always measure LF twice: Once with the brow neutralized to avoid false elevation.
In MMCR, resecting 8mm of tissue typically provides 2mm of elevation.
Avoid the Orbital Septum: If you suture it to the tarsus, you will cause lagophthalmos.
The 'Ice Test' for MG: 2 minutes of ice pack improves ptosis by 2mm+ in 80% of MG cases.
Pediatric Ptosis: If the lid covers the visual axis, surgery is an emergency to prevent stimulus-deprivation amblyopia.
